title: Event plus response
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which part of the event can you actually control?
A student recalled a formula from an earlier book: event plus response equals outcome. You cannot control the event, but you can control the response.

Another said: use a label; it is very bold, and people have the courage to say it. What interests me is the process: buying time, asking questions, then stepping back to figure out what they are saying.
Jose said that when someone comes to you with drama or a negative trigger and you respond emotionally, you lose; you want to validate them first.
He said you can have an aggressive person come to you and not only defuse the situation but control their emotional landscape, which he thinks is very powerful.
Jose said that he and two colleagues had been calling companies they did not know, speaking to top-level managers. A student said that of seventeen calls only one refused to hear them out.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a recent event you could not control.
Write the response you would choose.
Write a label you could use.
Write a time you will buy.

check.q: What is the formula the student recalled?
What did Jose say you do first with a negative trigger?
What did a student say is interesting?

recap: You cannot control the event. You can control your response.
